memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "All those who were skilled among the workers made the tabernacle with ten curtains of finely twisted linen and blue, purple and scarlet yarn, with cherubim woven into them by a skilled worker. All the curtains were the same size - twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide." - Exod 36:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The work begins, and immediately we are given measurements. Ten curtains. Twenty-eight cubits by four. All identical.

We might skim past this. But consider what it took. Ten enormous curtains, hand-woven, with cherubim figures worked into the fabric, every one matching exactly. No machines. No shortcuts. Months of patient labour by people whose names we do not know.

And most of this beauty would never be admired. The inner curtains hung where only priests would see them.

That tells us something about serving God. Excellence offered to Him does not depend on an audience. If God sees it, it is seen.

The cherubim woven into the fabric are significant too. Cherubim first appear guarding the way back to Eden after humanity was shut out (Gen 3:24). Now they are woven into the walls of the place where God would dwell among His people — a reminder of both holiness and the beginning of a way back.

That way opened fully at the cross, when the temple curtain was torn from top to bottom (Matt 27:51). The barrier the cherubim represented came down.

Do your work carefully, even where no one will look.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you work as carefully when no one is watching?
2. Where are you tempted to cut corners because it will not be noticed?
3. What does it mean to you that the curtain has been torn?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You see everything I do. Let my hidden work be as careful as my visible work. Amen.
